nodes.label: Prepare (track page tab) feature
nodes.rationale: The track page's Prepare tab: check and fix BPM and beat grid by ear, set cues and loops, try other tempos. Corrections override the analysis (ADR 0052). Milestone M4; status in-progress: steps 1 and 2 shipped 2026-09-26, step 3 (rekordbox XML export with cues and grid) next. Adrs: 0052, 0006, 0011, 0168, 0169, 0170, 0192.

nodes.label: Prepare waveform (overview and deck)
nodes.rationale: An overview of the whole track (click to seek) and a zoomed deck view scrolling under a fixed playhead. Colour schemes RGB (3-band, Rekordbox-like), Blue, Bands (stacked), Mono. The 3D view as on Details can be shown below it; it turns, zooms and resets (ADR 0073).

nodes.label: Prepare beat grid editing
nodes.rationale: Beat grid drawn behind the wave on both views, bar lines numbered and beats fainter. Edits: BPM plus or minus 0.01, times 2, divide by 2, tap tempo; nudge earlier or later; Beat 1 here at the playhead; Reset to analysis. Saved on the track and the beats renumbered so the bar lines stay put (core/library/grid.ts). Placed on the audio for the BPM in use; the onset detector's lag is corrected (ONSET_LAG, measured 18.6 ms); the downbeat is the loudest of each four beats.

nodes.label: Prepare BPM shown as
nodes.rationale: Per profile (profiles screen): as detected, half-time 60-120 or full 120-240. Per track: flip to the other octave. Copies of the same recording share the BPM correction, flip and Reset (a same-recording group in Duplicates); the grid is copied only to copies of the same length (within 10 ms). Details' Tempo card shows the corrected BPM with its source. Motivating case (2026-09-26): two files 20 bytes apart were two songs in the library, so the correction showed twice.

nodes.label: Prepare tempo fader and key lock
nodes.rationale: A pitch fader of plus or minus 8, 16 or 50 percent (double-click for 0), with key lock; the BPM shown follows the speed. Leaving the tab puts the speed back to normal.

nodes.label: Prepare metronome
nodes.rationale: Clicks on the grid with the accent on each bar's first beat, with its own volume. Scheduled on the music's own AudioContext 150 ms ahead (lib/metronome.ts). Not checked by a test: headless browsers have no audio out, so the clicks being heard in time must be checked by ear.

nodes.label: Prepare cues and loops
nodes.rationale: Hot cues A-H in Rekordbox's colours (click an empty pad to set, a set pad to jump, right-click or shift-click to clear; keys 1-8). Quantize (Q) on by default. Loops of 1 to 16 beats repeat while playing; Save loop keeps a memory loop. Memory cues are a list. Saved as Track.prep.cues (the CuePoint shape imports use); kept on re-analyse; copied to other copies only when they have the same length. Code in core/library/cueEdit.ts (pure, unit-tested); the panel is PrepareView.svelte.

nodes.label: Prepare cues and grids from the DJ apps
nodes.rationale: In your DJ apps (ADR 0168): each of this computer's DJ libraries' cues, loops and grid, from their records (SourceTrack.cueList, grid), read from rekordbox XML, Traktor and Engine DJ PerformanceData (core/interop/enginePerf.ts). The main DJ library (ADR 0169) is the song's default, GLUE's own first. Kept in step both ways with Engine DJ (ADR 0170): changes go into Engine DJ once it's closed; a song changed on both shows a banner with Keep GLUE's or Keep Engine DJ's. Next: playlists both ways with Engine DJ, then rekordbox.

nodes.label: Prepare data and the waveform job
nodes.rationale: Track.prep stores bpm, beat0 (first beat in seconds), bar (0-3), flip, and cues. lib/bpm.ts works out the BPM in use and the BPM shown. The waveform job (core/audio/waveform.ts, in the analysis worker) makes 3 bands at 150 points per second and the beat phase for the BPM in use; cached in the browser's storage per track, size and date. Its audio is decoded in the worker (ADR 0060) so opening Prepare does not hold the page.

nodes.label: Prepare tests
nodes.rationale: Unit: beat phase on synthetic clicks with a known offset, folding into ranges, prep reset. e2e (e2e/prepare.spec.ts) on a synthetic 30 s beat at 124 BPM: Prepare opens and the waveform draws; tempo +4 percent shows 128.96; the metronome toggles; a correction to 125 survives a reload; half-time shows 62.5 and the flip brings back 125; Re-analyse removes the correction.
